result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings, and fixed all of them. To check, I wrote a reference version of each rule from its docstring and compared it with the real function over many quantities (around each threshold and well above it) and unit prices. All 150 rules now match.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 02, 149 | Discount was rounded with `round()`, not floored | Changed to `base * pct // 100` |
| 15, 38, 89 | Marginal discount was rounded with `round()` | Changed to `(qty - th) * unit * pct // 100` |
| 32 | Used `qty > 5`, so exactly 5 units got no discount | Changed to `qty >= 5` |
| 74 | Threshold was 31 | Changed to `qty >= 30` |
| 60 | Capped the price before applying 10%, not the discount | Now takes 10% first, then caps the discount at 30,000 |
| 119 | Rate was 16% | Changed to 15% |
| 121 | Cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 | Discount now always capped at 30,000 |
| 126 | Rate was 11% | Changed to 10% |
| 140 | Computed as marginal, but the docstring says whole | Changed to `base * 3 // 100` |

STATUS: DONE
